In other words, it requires that:

P(i → j) = P(j → i) \* (P(j) / P(i))

where P(i → j) is the probability of transitioning from state i to state j, P(j → i) is the probability of transitioning from state j to state i, and P(i) and P(j) are the equilibrium probabilities of states i and j, respectively.

This condition ensures that the system is in equilibrium, meaning that the probability of being in each state is constant over time. Detailed Balance is an important concept in statistical mechanics, thermodynamics, and Markov chain theory.
